lines.quote: I implemented the near-field-to-far-field transform for the element array pattern, validated beamforming weight sets against measured data across the full 8–12 GHz operating band, and iterated the weight optimisation in Python before committing the production version to the embedded C++ firmware.
All processing firmware written in C++ targeting TI C6000 DSP processors under hard 50 µs cycle-time constraints; the pipeline has shipped in every LP-400 variant since 2007.

Grew from a personal utility into a CI-integrated package (v4.2), unit-tested with pytest, used daily by eight engineers on two product lines. Written and maintained as production Python — not one-off analysis scripting.

Measured S-parameters and radiation patterns with a Keysight PNA-X vector network analyser and the Oulujoki University anechoic chamber across 8–12 GHz, comparing measured element patterns against HFSS simulation models.

lines.quote: Co-authored "Wideband element-pattern calibration for sparse aperture arrays," Proc. Baltic Microwave Conference, 2019. Maintainer of aperture-utils, an open-source Python library for aperture-illumination analysis (~120 stars on GitHub).
Consortium participation terms required EU work authorisation, held as a Finnish citizen.
All internal documentation, design specifications, and test protocols written in English; English is the team's working language for all design reviews and external communication.
Based at Hohtola Photonics' Oulu headquarters since 2002. The entire sensor R&D division works onsite.

Oulu is home — I have lived and worked here since 2002, I know the local engineering community through the university's microwave-group seminars and the annual Polar Engineering workshop, and I have no intention of leaving.
